module_microarchitecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_microarchitecture.implementation_style: Single-clock synthesizable top-level control IP with a compact register window, shallow control-state request/response sequencing, response validation, deterministic bounded command generation, and telemetry reporting. The implementation should use simple synchronous registers, comparators, counters, clamp logic, and a small encoded or one-hot control state, without any inference or physics computation.
module_microarchitecture.control_strategy: Use the register bank to capture enable, mode, clear-fault, slew-enable, timeout/window, sequence tracking, setpoint/velocity estimate, and clamp bounds. Generate request metadata from configuration plus local state, advance outstanding-request tracking on accepted request handshakes, accept response metadata only on valid/ready handshakes, and mark responses stale on sequence mismatch or timeout/age violation. On any validation or bounds failure, select fallback behavior and latch fault status per the configured clear policy.
module_microarchitecture.state_strategy: Maintain a small set of synchronous control registers for configuration, outstanding request sequence, request age/timeout counter, latest accepted command, previous command for optional slew limiting, fault latch bits, clamp-activity flag, stale-data flag, timeout flag, and fallback-active flag. Keep any temporary response staging shallow and bounded; if payload staging is needed, map it to the explicitly specified SRAM macro contract rather than flattened registers.
module_microarchitecture.output_strategy: Drive req_stream_valid and req_stream_data from real top-level request-generation logic, drive rsp_stream_ready from top-level response-acceptance readiness, drive actuator_cmd_valid and actuator_cmd_data from the clamped and optionally slew-limited command path, and drive telemetry_out_valid and telemetry_out_data from latched status. All required top-level outputs must have explicit RTL drivers and remain deterministic under all conditions.
ownership_notes: This module is the design top and must not be substituted by a status, telemetry, register-bank, or leaf module.
It owns all externally visible outputs defined in the specification and must not rely on a child-only driver for any required top output.
External model transport direction follows the mandatory contract: the RTL emits request valid/data and receives request ready; the RTL receives response valid/data and emits response ready.
No neural inference, CFD, geometry processing, tensor arithmetic, or surrogate model computation is implemented here.

fsm_intent.description: A small synchronous control FSM is implied to coordinate reset-safe idle behavior, configuration readiness, request issuance, response acceptance, validation, command update, telemetry update, and fallback hold behavior. The FSM should remain simple and encoded rather than elaborate.

internal_storage: Compact configuration register bank for CTRL, STATUS, SEQ, TIMEOUT, SETPOINT, CMD_MIN, CMD_MAX, and SLEW
Previous actuator command for optional slew limiting
Fault latch and status flag bits
Optional shallow bounded response staging through the named SRAM macro if implementation requires temporary buffering
output_mapping: cfg_rdata[31:0] reflects selected register contents and status words
req_stream_valid and req_stream_data[127:0] reflect compact request metadata only
rsp_stream_ready indicates readiness to accept a valid compact response
actuator_cmd_valid and actuator_cmd_data[63:0] reflect the final bounded command after validation, clamping, and optional slew limiting
telemetry_out_valid and telemetry_out_data[31:0] reflect mode, active fault code, stale-data flag, timeout flag, clamp-activity flag, and fallback-active flag

sequencing_notes: On synchronous reset, clear configuration state, outstanding request tracking, response freshness tracking, timeout counters, error latches, clamp-activity indicators, fallback-selection state, and command history to safe defaults.
Do not assert actuation until the controller is configured and explicitly enabled.
Issue a compact request only when the controller is ready and the shallow control-state handshake policy allows it; keep payloads metadata-only.
Accept a response only on a successful valid/ready handshake, then compare its sequence and age against the latest outstanding request.
If the response sequence mismatches or the age/timeout threshold is exceeded, mark the response stale, latch fault status, and select fallback behavior.
Apply clamp logic to every actuator component before output issuance, and optionally apply slew limiting relative to the previous command when enabled.
Telemetry should be updated from latched top-level state so that status remains stable and deterministic across handshakes.
timing_notes: Single synchronous clk domain at 50 MHz; all counters, state transitions, and output register updates should be clocked on clk with synchronous active-low reset handling.
Avoid asynchronous combinational feedback across valid/ready interfaces.
Keep request/response staging shallow and bounded to preserve simple timing and avoid large inferred payload memories.
Use straightforward comparator and counter paths for sequence, timeout, clamp, and slew checks so the design remains FPGA-friendly.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
